clue.text: There's a big noise about me being one who wanders

indicators.note: the big noise is placed around the following word, so 'about' signals a container

parts.note: a roar is a big noise
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of being the loudest traveller around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's a big noise' reads as a statement, but the phrase is a single piece; 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover or wanderer is a person who travels about without fixed purpose.

clue.text: Desiring to get a seat in the front row

definitions.text: a seat in the front row

indicators.note: the letters of the first word are made to get into a new form, read here as a rearrangement signal

explanation.surface: Someone longs for the best seat at a boxing match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' is the loose anagram signal: DESIRING rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Seats at the edge of a boxing ring or arena are the closest to the action, in the very first row.

clue.text: Did she cause a bear to stir everything up?

indicators.note: to stir is to mix things up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: everything means all

explanation.surface: A question about a woman who riled a bear into a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' mixes BEAR and ALL into RABELLA; 'up' just completes the phrase 'stir up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so a woman fits the pronoun.

clue.text: Alienate the nasty sergeant

indicators.note: a nasty person is twisted out of shape, so the next word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to keep away from an unpleasant army NCO.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to drive them away and make them unfriendly.

clue.text: Relevant stuff.

explanation.surface: A note that the useful material is here.
explanation.definitionFit: Relevant evidence is pertinent to a case; stuff is the fabric or substance something is made from.

clue.text: It causes annoyance when operations have to be rearranged

indicators.note: rearranged plainly orders a new arrangement of the letters of the word beside it

explanation.surface: A grumble about surgery being rescheduled.
explanation.definitionFit: A touchy subject is something that irritates whenever it comes up.

clue.text: Show how former wife is so backward in keep fit

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse

indicators.note: 'in' puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school exercise

indicators.note: backward tells us to write the word so from right to left

parts.note: taken as written before turning

explanation.surface: Someone's ex-wife is shown to be slow at the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns SO into OS. PE is the usual school abbreviation for physical education; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal or lay bare the workings of something, demonstrating how it is done.

clue.text: Can't it be left untouched?

indicators.note: the letters are left in a new order, a loose anagram signal

explanation.surface: A plea to let something alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be left' rearranges the letters of CANT and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something whole and unharmed has been left undamaged.

clue.text: Fifty one untruths or bloomers

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
I is the Roman numeral for one
untruths are lies

explanation.surface: A count of fibs or embarrassing mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like mistakes or underwear, but means flowers, things that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowers are things that bloom, hence blooming plants.

clue.text: Not far behind 1 down perhaps

parts.note: 1 down is a ringside seat; such a seat is close to the very first line of spectators

explanation.surface: A remark about seating position at a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue refers to the answer to 1 down, a ringside seat, which is close to the action.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringside seats are placed in a position close by the leading row of an audience.

clue.text: People not well treated here

parts.note: reads as a complaint about poor service, but means sick people receive medical care in this place

explanation.surface: A complaint about bad service somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: An institution where the sick and injured receive medical care.

clue.text: Was about to look back so move up or down

parts.note: to look back on something is to see it again in the mind; here simply see

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word was is written backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning

explanation.surface: Someone about to glance back thinks better of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns WAS into SAW; 'back' merely suggests a glance behind. The definition is a verb, to rise and fall in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A playground plank pivoted in the middle rises and falls; as a verb it means oscillate.

clue.text: This demands a response in church

definitions.text: This demands a response in church

parts.words: This demands a response in church
parts.note: describes a short line said by a priest to which the congregation replies

explanation.surface: A reflection on church services needing an answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In liturgy, a short sentence said by the officiant, answered by the people.

clue.text: Puts up with the Oriental sound somehow; that's marvellous!

indicators.note: somehow suggests the pieces are arranged in some unspecified way

parts.note: E for East, the Orient

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates Eastern music and is amazed by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' jumbles PUTS, E and SOUND together.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazing or astounding, so wonderful.

clue.text: Do get a line sent to the embassy!

indicators.note: sent as in sent flying or sent mad, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: An urgent order to send a message to the embassy.
explanation.definitionFit: An embassy in its older sense is a deputation of envoys sent abroad.

clue.text: Suspect corrosion following fog

indicators.note: following places the corrosion word after the fog word

parts.note: mist is a light fog
rust is corrosion of iron

explanation.surface: Someone suspects rust has formed after damp weather.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect is to doubt or distrust someone.

clue.text: Calculating the ingredients for a pudding

indicators.note: the ingredients are the raw makings, here the letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Working out the recipe for a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ingredients for' rearranges PUDDING into DDINGUP, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Totting up figures is calculating a total.

clue.text: Lied about the head during a free period

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of lied are rearranged

parts.note: a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: Someone fibbed to the headteacher in a spare lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LIED as IDLE; NESS is a headland, often in Scottish place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Time spent not working is time of inactivity, so a period with nothing to do.

clue.text: Perhaps no MP denied being free from prejudice

indicators.note: perhaps suggests one possible version of the letters, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: A politician refusing a charge of bias.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unbiased and receptive to new ideas.

clue.text: Painful ache gives way to desire

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
an itch is a desire

explanation.surface: Pain subsides and a craving takes over.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp pain in the side, as from running.

clue.text: Raised a danger signal about the organ

indicators.note: the signal word goes around the organ word, so about signals a container

parts.note: red is the colour of danger
the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: An alarm sounded about some body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Brought up, as a child or animal is nurtured.

clue.text: Purple dye mixed in core

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of the following words are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: Colouring blended into the centre of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish-purple colouring obtained from lichens, used as a stain.

clue.text: See 9
Way to be carried — or walk

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
to ride is to be carried along

explanation.surface: A choice between being driven or going on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A long step is a manner of walking.

clue.text: Began to work when switch was pressed

definitions.text: Began to work when switch was pressed

parts.words: Began to work when switch was pressed
parts.note: describes a device activated by a switch

explanation.surface: A machine came on when the button was pushed.
explanation.definitionFit: A device is activated by flicking a switch.

clue.text: Give a plug to the French in a rather clumsy manner

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase defining a verb: to act in this manner

parts.note: to bung is to plug or stop up
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Advertising something in French very awkwardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give a plug' suggests publicity, but means stopping a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: To botch is to do something clumsily.

clue.text: He would send nothing back, in the way of a pleasure seeker

parts.note: contraction he'd
O is nought

indicators.note: back means the little word in is written right to left

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A man refusing to return anything, like a selfish person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone devoted to sensual enjoyment as the highest good.

clue.text: Stops round the point and excavates

indicators.note: the stops word goes round the point, so round signals a container

parts.note: E is east, a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone halts at a headland and digs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts E inside STOPS. To stope is a mining term for digging out ore in steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A mining verb meaning to dig ore from a stepped working.
